metadata.title: Teacher innovation: Conceptualizations, methodologies, and theoretical framework

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This study is a systematic review of 109 peer-reviewed articles on teacher innovation and does not analyze student-level ILSA microdata. Therefore, there is no sampling frame for students, schools, or countries and no application of TALIS sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures. The review follows PRISMA guidance and uses explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria for study selection rather than complex survey estimation. Any weighting concepts in the review refer to study-quality scoring and selection thresholds, not to survey-weighted achievement or PV-based estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because this is a systematic review that synthesizes published research on teacher innovation rather than analyzing ILSA cognitive achievement outcomes that use PVs. Missing-data handling is not reported because the authors do not perform statistical modeling on an individual-level dataset; instead, they conduct study screening, full-text eligibility assessment, and quality appraisal using PRISMA and Petticrew & Roberts criteria.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Systematic review selection: searched seven databases (Web of Science, ERIC, ScienceDirect, Taylor & Francis, Emerald, Sage, Springer) using teacher-innovation/creativity keywords; removed duplicates; screened titles/abstracts; included only peer-reviewed international journal articles in English published before 31 Dec 2023; excluded studies with pre-service/tertiary teachers, non-primary focus on teacher innovation, non-English publications, and studies failing quality criteria. Full-text eligibility required teacher innovation as primary focus and in-service teachers in primary, secondary, or vocational schools; quality appraisal used 11 criteria with a minimum total score of 5.5 (3-point scale) based on Petticrew & Roberts (2006).

data.outcome_summary: This article is a systematic review (PRISMA-guided) synthesizing 109 studies on teacher innovation, including 96 empirical studies (69 quantitative, 22 qualitative, 5 mixed-methods) plus 13 additional excluded/quality-screened records during selection. It does not train or evaluate machine-learning models on TALIS or any other ILSA microdata; instead, it reports descriptive synthesis results about how teacher innovation is conceptualized, measured, and studied. The review finds that teacher innovation definitions are inconsistent (with 23.7% of reviewed papers not providing a definition), that measurement often relies on self-report scales with variable psychometric rigor, and that quantitative studies heavily favor cross-sectional designs and advanced statistical approaches while underusing longitudinal designs. It also highlights limited theoretical integration (only 7.3% explicitly used theories) and calls for stronger measurement, more diverse data sources, and better theoretical grounding. Limitations include potential omission of relevant non-English or non-journal sources and manual coding subjectivity.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a review article without original student-level ILSA microdata analysis. As a result, there are no PVs, no ML model training/evaluation, no country-level student counts, and no survey-weighting or missing-data procedures to extract from an analytic dataset. The study’s “sample” refers to the number of included publications and their study-level characteristics, not to an ILSA respondent dataset.
